notes:
I couldn't do this research, so I have no notes for you. My only way to reach the web is blocked: every attempt to fetch a page, starting with Enduring Word's Proverbs 1 commentary, failed with a message saying I have no tool calls left for this turn. My other tools have no internet access.

You asked me to report only what the pages actually say, with a URL for each point. I could write verse notes on Proverbs 1 from memory, but I would have to make up citations, so I haven't.

**Planned sources for when access is back:**
- **Verse-by-verse (traditional reading):** enduringword.com/bible-commentary/proverbs-1/; preceptaustin.org's Proverbs 1 commentary; the Gill, Ellicott, Pulpit, Barnes and Benson notes on biblehub.com; Wesley's notes on studylight.org.
- **Where Protestant traditions differ:**
  - Verses 23–29, where wisdom says "I would have poured out my spirit" and "you refused my call." The question is whether grace can be resisted. I'd compare Wesley's notes and Seedbed against Gill, Ligonier and Monergism.
  - Verse 23 as a pointer to the Holy Spirit, for Pentecostal and charismatic readings on enduringword.com and ag.org.
  - Verse 7, "the fear of the LORD." I'd look at what Desiring God, GTY and the Lutheran sites (lcms.org, 1517.org) say about fear and faith.
- **Other views:**
  - NET Bible translators' notes on hard words, such as the terms for "simple," "scoffer" and "fool," and the "spirit" in verse 23.
  - Bible Odyssey on Woman Wisdom (verses 20–33).
  - Catholic and Orthodox readings of Wisdom as Christ, the divine Logos, on newadvent.org (Church Fathers) and oca.org.
  - Popular modern teaching, such as prosperity readings of verses 13 and 33, as described on GotQuestions or Ligonier.

If you try again in a new message, I'll start with those pages. If you need it sooner, you could paste in text from any of these pages and I'll write the verse-by-verse notes from that, citing each point.
